title: VOID PVP — Mod registry
description: The closed registry of the 13 mods VOID ships — the 12 defined in PVP_ARCHITECTURE.md §3 plus the VOID watermark — together with the per-mod settings sub-schema, the anti-cheat classification of §11, the Mods-panel `category` taxonomy of Figma 244:538 and the factory defaults. This file is the single source of truth for mod identity, display copy and classification: `loadout.json` and `bridge.json` both $ref its `mod_id` enum and its `<id>_settings` definitions, so a mod is added in exactly one place, and no consumer re-declares a label or a filter tab. An instance of this schema is a registry document; the registry VOID actually ships is `examples[0]`.
$comment: GENERATED by schema/build.mjs from schema/mods/*.json — do not edit by hand. A mod is added by writing one file, schema/mods/<id>.json, and re-running the script. `node build.mjs --check` is the CI gate that this file matches its sources.

version.title: Registry version
version.description: Integer revision of the registry document. Bumped whenever a mod is added, removed or reclassified. Independent of the wire protocol version `v` in protocol.json.

mods.title: Mods
mods.description: Every mod VOID ships, keyed by its snake_case mod id. Closed set: all 14 keys are required and no others are permitted.

mod_id.title: Mod id
mod_id.description: Closed enum of the 14 mods of §3, snake_case. Used as the key of `loadout.mods`, as the `id` argument of `void.setModSetting`, and as the id of a HUD item.

hud_mod_id.title: HUD mod id
hud_mod_id.description: The subset of mod ids whose `kind` is `hud`, i.e. the 9 mods that own a draggable HUD item. A mod may only appear in `loadout.hud` if it is listed here.

gameplay_mod_id.title: Gameplay mod id
gameplay_mod_id.description: The subset of mod ids whose `kind` is `gameplay`, i.e. the mods an actuator Mixin reads every frame. These are the only ids accepted by `void.setGameplay`.

kind.title: Mod kind
kind.description: Data direction of the mod, per §3. `hud` mods only read game state and draw; `gameplay` mods mutate a documented client-side option through an actuator Mixin.

category.title: Mod category
category.description: The product taxonomy the Mods panel filters across — the tabs `All / HUD / PvP / Visual / Utility` of Figma 244:538, and the tag printed on each tile. Distinct from `kind`, which is a data-direction split (does the mod draw, or does it mutate a client-side option): Crosshair is `kind: gameplay` but `category: visual`, and Zoom is `kind: gameplay` but `category: utility`. Carried here so no consumer has to hard-code the mapping.

key_swatch.title: Key colour swatch
key_swatch.description: One of the five unpressed-key swatches on the Mod settings frame, named by the design token it resolves to (`--bg-shell`, `--surface-2`, `--surface-3`, `--sky`, `--teal`). A name rather than a hex value so the choice survives a theme change.

pressed_swatch.title: Pressed colour swatch
pressed_swatch.description: One of the five pressed-key swatches on the Mod settings frame, named by the design token it resolves to (`--accent`, `--sky`, `--warn`, `--danger`, `--teal`). `accent` is the frame's default and follows the loadout accent.

hypixel_safe.title: Hypixel safety class
hypixel_safe.description: Anti-cheat posture of §11. `safe` mods are unambiguously allowed; `grey` mods change what the player can see and are tolerated but not endorsed. The HYPIXEL-READY badge is shown only when every enabled mod in the loadout is `safe`.

keybind.title: Keybind
keybind.description: An LWJGL 2 key name in upper case as used by Minecraft 1.8.9 `Keyboard.getKeyName`, a mouse button as MOUSE0..MOUSE7, or NONE for unbound. Produced by `void.openKeybindCapture`.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Multiplier applied to the mod's rendered size, on top of MC GUI scale x window DPI (§6.2). 1 is the design size.

opacity.title: Opacity
opacity.description: Alpha of the mod's rendered element, 0 fully transparent to 1 fully opaque.

hex_color.title: Colour
hex_color.description: sRGB colour as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. Lower case or upper case hex both accepted.

on.title: Enabled
on.description: Whether the mod is enabled. Present in every mod state inside a loadout, and in the registry `defaults` as the factory enabled state.

mod_entry.title: Registry entry
mod_entry.description: One row of the §3 table plus its §11 classification and factory defaults. Every key is listed here; the per-mod entry definitions narrow `id`, `kind`, `hypixel_safe` and `defaults` to constants.

id.description: The mod's snake_case id; equals the key this entry is stored under.

kind.description: Whether this mod draws (hud) or mutates a client-side option (gameplay).

category.description: Filter-tab taxonomy of the Mods panel, per frame 244:538.

label.description: Human-readable name as it appears in the Mods panel of the Figma.

icon.description: Name of the glyph the Mods list and the quick palette draw for this mod, from `@void/ui`'s icon sheet. Carried here rather than in a table per application: the in-game overlay and the desktop launcher both need it and neither can import the other, so before this it was one hand-maintained `MOD_ICONS` object that no schema knew about. Not consumed by the game — the mod draws no icons — but the registry is where mod *identity* lives, and an icon is identity.

description.description: One-line explanation shown under the label in the Mods panel.

source.description: The Minecraft 1.8.9 field, method or injection point the sensor reads or the actuator writes, quoted from the §3 table. Documentation only; not consumed at runtime.

defaults.description: Factory settings for this mod, used when a loadout omits it. Validates against the mod's own settings sub-schema.

fps_settings.title: FPS display settings
fps_settings.description: Settings for the FPS display HUD mod. Reads `Minecraft.debugFPS` once per tick.

on.description: Whether the FPS display is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the FPS tile.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the FPS tile, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

border.description: Whether a hairline is drawn around the FPS tile, at the system's own `--border-panel` alpha. Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

padding.description: Density of the FPS tile — the inset between its content and its edge, as one of three steps. `density` is named in §1 as legitimate customisation, and it is what a player actually means by 'make the HUD smaller' when `scale` has already made the text too small to read.

color.description: Text colour of the FPS readout.

show_label.description: Whether to render the trailing "FPS" label after the number.

show_low.description: Whether the 1% low is drawn as a trailing aside. It is the figure that says whether a frame rate is actually smooth, and it is also a third number on the chip a player reads mid-match — so it is a switch rather than something that appears whenever a low has been measured.

keystrokes_settings.title: Keystrokes settings
keystrokes_settings.description: Settings for the Keystrokes HUD mod. Fed by the edge-triggered `keys` bridge event (§6.5), never by polling.

on.description: Whether the keystrokes overlay is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the key tiles.

opacity.description: Alpha of the key tiles when a key is not pressed.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the key tiles, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

border.description: Whether a hairline is drawn around the key tiles, at the system's own `--border-panel` alpha. Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

padding.description: Density of the key tiles — the inset between its content and its edge, as one of three steps. `density` is named in §1 as legitimate customisation, and it is what a player actually means by 'make the HUD smaller' when `scale` has already made the text too small to read.

keybind.description: Optional key that toggles the keystrokes overlay on and off in game without opening the menu. NONE leaves it always visible while the mod is on.

show_mouse.description: Whether to render the LMB and RMB tiles under the WASD block.

show_spacebar.description: Whether to render the spacebar tile.

show_sneak.description: Whether to render the sneak (shift) tile beside the space bar. The `keys` event has always carried `shift` and the widget has always been handed it; this is the switch that draws it. A sneak key is as much a part of reading a PvP player's inputs as the space bar, which is why the two sit together.

show_cps.description: Whether to print the current CPS inside the LMB and RMB tiles.

corner_radius.description: Corner radius of a key tile in unscaled GUI pixels, drawn as the `Corner radius` slider on the Mod settings frame (Figma 244:834). 0 is a square tile.

key_color.description: Background of an unpressed key tile, as one of the five named swatches the Mod settings frame offers. A token name rather than a hex value, so the tile keeps following the theme when the theme changes.

pressed_color.description: Fill of a pressed key tile, as one of the five named swatches the Mod settings frame offers. `accent` follows the loadout accent, which is the frame's default.

cps_settings.title: CPS counter settings
cps_settings.description: Settings for the CPS counter HUD mod. Derived entirely in JS from mouse edges on the `keys` event (§3), so no Java sensor exists for it.

on.description: Whether the CPS counter is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the CPS tile.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the CPS tile, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

mode.description: Which mouse buttons to count: left only, right only, or both shown side by side.

show_label.description: Whether to render the trailing "CPS" unit after the figures. Every other readout on the HUD can drop its unit; this one could not, which left it the widest chip on screen for a player who already knows what the number is.

window_ms.description: Length of the sliding window in milliseconds over which clicks are counted before being scaled to clicks per second.

ping_settings.title: Ping display settings
ping_settings.description: Settings for the Ping display HUD mod. Reads the player's own `NetworkPlayerInfo.responseTime`.

on.description: Whether the ping display is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the ping tile.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the ping tile, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. show_label.description: Whether to render the trailing "ms" unit after the number.

good_ms.description: Ping at or below this many milliseconds renders in the good colour.

bad_ms.description: Ping at or above this many milliseconds renders in the bad colour. Must be greater than `good_ms`; not enforced by the schema.

show_host.description: Whether the shortened server name is drawn after the figure. A player who only ever plays one server is being told something they already know, on the chip they look at most often.

coordinates_settings.title: Coordinates settings
coordinates_settings.description: Settings for the Coordinates HUD mod. Reads `EntityPlayerSP` position and yaw once per tick.

on.description: Whether the coordinates display is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the coordinates tile.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the coordinates tile, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

border.description: Whether a hairline is drawn around the coordinates tile, at the system's own `--border-panel` alpha. Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

padding.description: Density of the coordinates tile — the inset between its content and its edge, as one of three steps. `density` is named in §1 as legitimate customisation, and it is what a player actually means by 'make the HUD smaller' when `scale` has already made the text too small to read.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places printed for X, Y and Z. Capped at 2 because that is what the wire carries: the `tick` sensor rounds the position to 2 dp before publishing it, so a third place could only ever print a zero. Widening it is a bridge change, not a settings change, and a costly one — 3 dp makes ten times as many positions distinct, and every distinct position is a HUD repaint.

show_direction.description: Whether to append the cardinal direction derived from yaw.

layout.description: Whether X, Y and Z are stacked on three lines or printed on one. Defaults to `inline`, which is what the HUD frame draws; `stacked` holds the three numbers against one left edge, which is easier to read while moving.

armor_status_settings.title: Armor status settings
armor_status_settings.description: Settings for the Armor status HUD mod. Reads `InventoryPlayer.armorInventory` durability, pushed only when it changes.

on.description: Whether the armor status display is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the armor row.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the armor row, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

orientation.description: Whether armor pieces are laid out left to right or top to bottom.

show_durability.description: Whether to print remaining durability as a number under each piece.

show_held_item.description: Whether to include the currently held item as a sixth slot.

warn_below.description: Fraction of maximum durability under which a piece's bar turns amber. A threshold on a live value, the same species as `ping.good_ms`: the point at which a player wants to be told their gear is going is a matter of how they play, not a constant. 0 never warns.

potion_effects_settings.description: Settings for the Potion effects HUD mod. Reads `getActivePotionEffects`, pushed only when the set changes.

on.description: Whether the potion effects display is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the effect list.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the effect list, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. show_duration.description: Whether to print the remaining duration next to each effect.

show_amplifier.description: Whether to print the roman-numeral amplifier next to each effect name.

hide_ambient.description: Whether to omit ambient effects such as a beacon aura from the list.

watermark_settings.title: VOID watermark settings
watermark_settings.description: Settings for the VOID watermark HUD mod. It reads nothing from the game: the overlay draws the mark itself, which is why its `source` says so rather than naming a 1.8.9 field. Modelled on `fps_settings` and `crosshair_settings`, and deliberately without a `color`: `design/quiet-cell-system.md` §1 reserves colour for a live value or a selected item, and a watermark is neither.

opacity.description: Alpha of the mark. Lower than the other HUD mods by default, so it sits behind the readouts the player is actually reading.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the mark, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

border.description: Whether a hairline is drawn around the mark, at the system's own `--border-panel` alpha. Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

padding.description: Density of the mark — the inset between its content and its edge, as one of three steps. `density` is named in §1 as legitimate customisation, and it is what a player actually means by 'make the HUD smaller' when `scale` has already made the text too small to read.

style.description: Which parts of the mark are drawn: `full` is the ring plus the VOID wordmark, `mark` is the ring alone, `word` is the wordmark alone.

toggle_sprint_settings.title: Toggle sprint settings
toggle_sprint_settings.description: Settings for the Toggle sprint gameplay mod. Overrides the sprint `KeyBinding` in `onLivingUpdate`.

mode.description: `toggle` latches sprint until the key is pressed again; `hold` restores vanilla hold-to-sprint but keeps the status readout.

sneak_too.description: Whether the same latching behaviour is applied to sneak.

fullbright_settings.title: Fullbright settings
fullbright_settings.description: Settings for the Fullbright gameplay mod. Overrides `gameSettings.gammaSetting`; client-side only and Watchdog-tolerated (§3), but classified `grey` in §11.

gamma.description: Value written to `gammaSetting` while the mod is on. Vanilla's slider tops out at 1; 10 is the conventional fullbright value.

hitboxes_settings.title: Hitboxes settings
hitboxes_settings.description: Settings for the Hitboxes gameplay mod. Forces `RenderManager.debugBoundingBox`. Classified `grey` in §11.

line_width.description: GL line width used for the bounding box wireframe.

color.description: Colour of the bounding box wireframe.

show_eye_line.description: Whether to draw the vanilla eye-direction ray along with the box.

zoom_settings.title: Zoom settings
zoom_settings.description: Settings for the Zoom gameplay mod. Overrides FOV while `key` is held.

key.description: Key held to zoom. Captured through `void.openKeybindCapture('zoom')`.

fov_divisor.description: The player's FOV is divided by this factor while zoomed. 4 approximates the familiar Optifine zoom.

smooth.description: Whether the FOV change is eased over a few frames rather than snapping.

cinematic.description: Whether smooth-camera mouse damping is applied while zoomed.

crosshair_settings.title: Crosshair settings
crosshair_settings.description: Settings for the Crosshair mod. Uniquely among the 13 it is drawn in GL rather than HTML (§3 footnote) because it must sit at the exact pixel centre, but it is configured through the same loadout model as everything else.

on.description: Whether the vanilla crosshair pass is replaced.

style.description: Shape drawn at the screen centre.

size.description: Half-length in pixels of each crosshair arm, before GUI scale.

thickness.description: Stroke thickness in pixels, before GUI scale.

gap.description: Empty gap in pixels between the centre point and the start of each arm.

outline.description: Whether a one-pixel black outline is drawn around the shape for contrast.

dynamic.description: Whether the gap widens while the attack cooldown is not full and while sprinting.

center_dot.description: Whether a dot of `thickness` square is drawn on the centre point, under whatever `style` draws around it. `dot` is a style, so without this a player must choose between a cross and a centre reference; every crosshair configurator worth the name lets them have both. Ignored by `none`, and by `default`, which is the vanilla pass.

direction_settings.title: Direction settings
direction_settings.description: Settings for the Direction HUD mod. Reads the same `pos.yaw` the tick sensor already sends for Coordinates, so it needs no sensor of its own — which is the whole reason it is cheap to ship. `coordinates.show_direction` is deliberately kept: that is the inline form, a suffix on the coordinate rows, and this is the standalone one a player places on its own and reads at a glance. Both are wanted, they are not duplicates of each other, and neither reads the other's settings.

on.description: Whether the direction display is enabled.

scale.description: Size multiplier of the direction chip.

background.description: Ground drawn behind the direction chip, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

border.description: Whether a hairline is drawn around the direction chip, at the system's own `--border-panel` alpha. Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

padding.description: Density of the direction chip — the inset between its content and its edge, as one of three steps. `density` is named in §1 as legitimate customisation, and it is what a player actually means by 'make the HUD smaller' when `scale` has already made the text too small to read.

style.description: How the facing is written. `letter` is the compass abbreviation the Coordinates mod already prints (`N`, `NE`, `SW`) and is what fits a small chip. `word` spells it out (`North`), which is what a player reading at a glance across a screen actually parses. `axis` prints the Minecraft world axis instead (`+X`, `-Z`) — not a compass reading at all, and the one a player wants while running a nether tunnel or lining up a build, because it is the notation coordinates themselves are in.

show_degrees.description: Whether the raw yaw angle is printed after the facing. Off by default: it is a second number on a chip whose whole job is to be read without reading, and it is only wanted by players aligning something precisely.
